# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030 and £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, providing NHS dentistry for all, boosting staff pay, and opposing privatisation. Mental health services would receive equal priority to physical health, with 28-day access to therapies. A National Cancer Control Plan and measures to end new HIV cases by 2030 are included.

## Social Care
The party proposes £20bn annual investment in social care, introducing free personal care modelled on Scotland's system, establishing national pay structures for care workers, and increasing children's social care funding by £3bn.

## Housing
Plans include building 150,000 social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, enabling local rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and investing £29bn over five years in home insulation. Planning reforms would protect green spaces while ensuring new developments include necessary infrastructure.

## Energy and Climate
The manifesto targets 70% wind-powered electricity by 2030, opposing new oil and gas licences while ending fossil fuel subsidies. A carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne would be introduced. Nuclear power development would cease. Community energy ownership would be prioritised, with investment in grid expansion and storage.

## Economy and Taxation
Proposed changes include a wealth tax (1% on assets over £10m, 2% over £1bn), aligning capital gains tax with income tax rates, and introducing a carbon tax. An average £40bn annual green investment programme is proposed. Water companies and railways would return to public ownership. The manifesto estimates raising £50-70bn annually through tax reforms.

## Employment
Proposals include a £15 minimum wage regardless of age, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, repealing anti-union legislation, and movement toward a four-day working week. Gig economy workers would receive full employment rights.

## Welfare
Universal Credit and legacy benefits would increase by £40 weekly. The two-child benefit cap would be abolished, disability benefits increased by 5%, and carer's allowance raised by 10%. The five-week benefit wait and bedroom tax would end.

## Environment
A Rights of Nature Act would give nature legal personhood. Targets include protecting 30% of land and sea by 2030, rewetting peatland, and banning harmful pesticides. Water companies would be nationalised. A new Right to Roam Act would improve nature access.

## Education
Proposals include £8bn additional school funding, abolishing tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, and investing £5bn in SEND provision. Academies would return to local authority control. Private school charitable status would end.

## Transport
Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10bn, with railways returning to public ownership. Investment includes £2.5bn annually for cycling and walking infrastructure. Sales of new petrol and diesel vehicles would end by 2027. A frequent-flyer levy and ban on short domestic flights are proposed.

## Democracy
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, an elected second chamber replacing the Lords, and repealing the Elections Act 2022. Local government funding would increase by £5bn annually.

## Immigration
The manifesto proposes ending the hostile environment, establishing safe asylum routes, permitting asylum seekers to work during applications, and abolishing minimum income requirements for spousal visas.

## Foreign Policy
Key positions include supporting an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire, recognising Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI, and working toward rejoining the EU. The party supports signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while remaining in NATO with reforms.

## Financing
Total additional spending in 2025-26 is projected at £122bn (£99bn revenue, £23bn capital), funded through £37bn in new taxes and £85bn additional borrowing, with deficit decreasing as carbon tax revenue increases.
